The `ArrayUtils.add` method in the Apache Commons Lang library is responsible for adding an element to an array. It performs some checks to determine the type of the array to be created and then adds the element accordingly.

Looking at the failing test case `org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtilsAddTest.testLANG571`, it initializes a `String[]` array and a `String` element as `null`. It then attempts to add the element to the array using `ArrayUtils.add(stringArray, aString)`, expecting an `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown.

The current bug report indicates that `ArrayUtils.add` can create an unexpected `ClassCastException` when both parameters are `null`. This is because if both parameters are `null`, the `add` method returns an `Object[]` array instead of the expected array type, leading to the exception.

Based on the code snippet of `ArrayUtils.add`, we can see that the method determines the type of the array to be created based on the non-null parameter between the array and the element. If both parameters are `null`, it defaults to creating an `Object[]` array, resulting in the unexpected behavior described in the bug report.

To fix this issue, we need to update the `ArrayUtils.add` method to handle the case where both parameters are `null` and ensure that the correct array type is created in such scenarios.

Next, I will provide the methods that should be fixed to address this issue.
`org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
